Subject: SIG follow-up — data handling specifics (prompt logs / training)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the SIG spreadsheet you sent earlier. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the initial answers and asked for a couple of clarifications around how Redwood treats customer prompts and derived artifacts. Can you confirm the following in plain language (we need to include these as evidence for our privacy review):

1) Are raw prompt/request bodies ever persisted beyond short-term debugging windows? If yes, what are default TTLs and can customers set them to zero?
2) Do you ever ingest customer prompts or outputs into model training datasets or fine-tuning pipelines? If so, under what contractual terms or opt-in mechanisms?
3) What logging tiers exist (debug, audit, metrics) and which tier would include PII or PHI? Please indicate retention windows for each.
4) Is there a formal customer-facing attestation we can present to our privacy/commercial teams stating that MediBridge data will not be used for training unless explicitly opted in?

We're on a tight procurement timeline — if possible we'd like a short PDF we can attach to our legal review. Appreciate any attachments or short attestations.

Best,
Lisa

Head of Security Operations | MediBridge Health

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear list. I've consolidated answers below and attached a short PDF attestation for your legal/privacy team. Quick summary up front: default behavior is ephemeral capture for operational/debugging only, customer data is not used for training by default, and there is an explicit opt-in contract path plus a signed attestation you can use. Details follow.

1) Raw prompt/request bodies:
- Default: request/response bodies are held in an encrypted, ephemeral cache for troubleshooting and performance telemetry. Default TTL is 48 hours.
- Customer control: Customers can configure retention to as low as 0 hours (no request body persisted) at the tenant level via the Console or API; we call this the "no-persist" mode.
- Access: Only redwood support and on-call engineers can access raw captures, and only via audited workflow and with JIRA ticket linkage for troubleshooting. Full access logs retained 1 year.

2) Use in model training:
- Policy: Redwood does not use any customer-specific prompts, outputs, or uploads to train public or private models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a signed agreement and technical opt-in flag.
- Technical enforcement: Training ingestion pipelines are gated; we maintain a tokenized allowlist per-tenant. Opt-in requires both legal counterparty signature and a toggle enabled in the customer's private control plane.
- Evidence: Attached: "Training_OptOut_Attestation.pdf" (signed standard attestation we provide for enterprise customers).

3) Logging tiers & retention:
- Debug captures: may include full request/response for debugging. Default retention 48 hours; configurable 0–168 hours. Contains any PII/PHI present in the request body if the customer provided it. Stored encrypted at rest.
- Audit logs (authn/authz, configuration changes): retained 365 days by default, contains identity/actor metadata but not full prompt contents.
- Aggregated metrics (latency, token counts): retained 3 years for billing and capacity planning; these are aggregated and not reversible to prompt contents.

4) Customer attestation:
- Attached PDF is our standard data-handling attestation you can present to Legal. It explicitly states we will not include MediBridge data in training datasets absent opt-in.

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_DataHandling_Responses_20260709.pdf (10 pages), Retention_Matrix_20260709.xlsx, Training_OptOut_Attestation.pdf

If you want, we can also provide a short one-paragraph statement for procurement that they can paste into their contract redlines. Happy to hop on a quick call today if you prefer.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
